title: Smart pointers: Box, Rc, Arc, and Mutex

questions.prompt: Which statement gives the core rule for “Smart pointers: Box, Rc, Arc, and Mutex”?
options: Arc shares ownership across threads; Mutex serializes mutable access to the critical section.
Rust bindings are immutable unless declared mut.
Cargo is the main tool for creating, building, and testing projects.
Use rustup to keep toolchain updates and installed versions explicit.
questions.answer: Arc shares ownership across threads; Mutex serializes mutable access to the critical section.
questions.explanation:
Arc shares ownership across threads; Mutex serializes mutable access to the critical section.
Why: Box<T> stores a value on the heap and enables recursive structures with a fixed-size pointer. Rc<T> provides reference-counted sharing within one thread; Arc<T> uses an atomic count for cross-thread sharing, but neither makes shared mutation automatically safe. Mutable shared state needs synchronization such as Mutex/RwLock and careful lock scopes.
